17	INSTALL_DIR="${FIZEAU_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"
18	SHELL_NAME=""

21	# Logging functions (all to stderr to avoid polluting command substitution)
22	log() {
23	    echo -e "${BLUE}[${BINARY_NAME}]${NC} $1" >&2
24	}

51	# Detect platform
52	detect_platform() {
53	    OS="$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
54	    ARCH="$(uname -m)"
55	
56	    case "$ARCH" in
57	        x86_64|amd64) ARCH="amd64" ;;
58	        aarch64|arm64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
59	        *) error "Unsupported architecture: $ARCH" ;;
60	    esac
61	
62	    case "$OS" in
63	        linux|darwin) ;;
64	        *) error "Unsupported OS: $OS" ;;
65	    esac
66	
67	    BINARY="${BINARY_NAME}-${OS}-${ARCH}"

70	# Get latest release tag
71	get_latest_release() {
72	    log "Fetching latest release..."
73	    
74	    if [ -n "${FIZEAU_VERSION:-}" ]; then
75	        TAG="${FIZEAU_VERSION}"
76	        # Normalize to tag format (add v prefix if missing)
77	        if [[ ! "$TAG" =~ ^v ]]; then
78	            TAG="v${TAG}"
79	        fi
80	        log "Using requested version: ${TAG}"
81	    else
82	        if command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
83	            TAG=$(curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}/releases/latest" | grep '"tag_name"' | sed -E 's/.*"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
84	        elif command -v wget &>/dev/null; then
85	            TAG=$(wget -qO- "https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}/releases/latest" | grep '"tag_name"' | sed -E 's/.*"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
86	        fi
87	
88	        if [ -z "$TAG" ]; then
89	            error "Could not determine latest release. Set FIZEAU_VERSION to specify a version."
90	        fi
91	        
92	        log "Latest release: ${TAG}"
93	    fi
94	    
95	    echo "$TAG"
96	}

98	# Download and install binary
99	install_binary() {
100	    local TAG="$1"
101	    
102	    URL="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases/download/${TAG}/${BINARY}"
103	    
104	    log "Installing ${BINARY_NAME} ${TAG} (${OS}/${ARCH})..."
105	    
106	    # Create installation directory
107	    mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR"
108	    
109	    # Download binary
110	    if command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
111	        curl -fsSL "$URL" -o "${INSTALL_DIR}/${BINARY_NAME}"
112	    elif command -v wget &>/dev/null; then
113	        wget -q "$URL" -O "${INSTALL_DIR}/${BINARY_NAME}"
114	    fi
115	    
116	    # Make executable
117	    chmod +x "${INSTALL_DIR}/${BINARY_NAME}"

119	    success "Installed ${BINARY_NAME} to ${INSTALL_DIR}/${BINARY_NAME}"
120	}

9	Fizeau is a Go library that implements a coding agent runtime - a tool-calling
10	LLM loop with file read/write, shell execution, navigation helpers, and
11	structured I/O. Designed to be embedded in
12	[DDx](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx) and other build orchestrators.
13	Prioritizes local model inference via LM Studio and Ollama, with transparent
14	escalation to cloud providers.

116	## Features
117	
118	- **Embeddable library** — `fizeau.New(...).Execute(ctx, request)`, no subprocess overhead
119	- **Local-model-first** — LM Studio, Ollama via OpenAI-compatible API
120	- **Multi-provider** — OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Claude, virtual (test replay)
121	- **9 built-in tools** — read, write, edit, bash, find, grep, ls, patch, task
122	- **Session logging** — JSONL with replay and cost tracking
123	- **System prompt composition** — pi-style builder with context file discovery
124	- **Standalone CLI** — `fiz -p "prompt"` with config, logging, replay

61	### Non-interactive invocation
62	
63	`pi -p` (`--print`) is the documented non-interactive mode: process prompt
64	and exit, no TTY. Combined with `--mode json` the harness emits one
65	JSON-line-per-event on stdout, which `internal/harnesses/pi/runner.go`
66	already parses (see `runStreaming` at `internal/harnesses/pi/runner.go:171`).
67	
68	For Harbor adapter use:
69	
70	```sh
71	pi --mode json --print --no-session \
72	   --provider <provider> --model <model> \
73	   [--thinking <level>] \
74	   "<prompt>"               # prompt as last positional arg
75	# or
76	pi --mode json --print --no-session ... < /dev/null   # if prompt comes via stdin
77	```
78	
79	- **No-TTY safe:** `--print` is the explicit non-interactive switch; pi does
80	  not call `isatty()` to gate behavior in this mode.
81	- **Stdin handling:** the adapter should attach `/dev/null` to stdin unless
82	  it intentionally pipes the prompt. Pi's interactive mode reads stdin; in
83	  `--print` mode it does not, so `/dev/null` is safe and recommended.
84	- **Exit-on-done:** `--print` exits 0 on success, non-zero on auth /
85	  provider failure. `--no-session` prevents writing session files into the
86	  task workdir, which would otherwise leak across reps.

187	| `provider.base_url`                   | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` `provider.<id>.options.baseURL` (JSON config; no CLI flag). The adapter writes this file on first run from the profile. |

193	The adapter's `apply_profile()` writes a minimal `opencode.json` per run
194	into a per-cell ephemeral `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=<cell-tmp>` so cells don't
195	contend on `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.
196	
197	### Custom base URL / OpenAI-compat / OpenRouter routing
198	
199	Opencode has first-class OpenAI-compat support via its provider plugin
200	system. For OpenRouter:
201	
202	```jsonc
203	// $OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/opencode.json
204	{
205	  "provider": {
206	    "openrouter": {
207	      "npm": "@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider",
208	      "options": { "apiKey": "{env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" },
209	      "models": { "qwen/qwen3.6-plus": {} }
210	    }
211	  }
212	}
213	```
214	
215	then `opencode run -m openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-plus ...`. The adapter
216	generates this JSON from the profile YAML; `provider.type: openai-compat` +
217	`base_url` + `api_key_env` map to a generic `openai-compat` provider entry.
218	
219	### Known limitations
220	
221	- **Profile cleanup:** opencode writes session DBs into
222	  `$OPENCODE_DATA_DIR` (defaults to `~/.local/share/opencode`). Adapter
223	  must override `OPENCODE_DATA_DIR=<cell-tmp>` and clean it between reps —
224	  otherwise rep-2 starts with rep-1's session cache and the matrix is
225	  contaminated.
226	- **Auto-update:** stock `opencode` checks for updates on launch over
227	  HTTPS; this is undesirable in a benchmark cell. Adapter sets

229	  loading) for hermeticity.

237	- **No CLI for max_output_tokens / temperature** — must go through the

7	# Feature Specification: FEAT-007 — Self-Update and Installer
8	
9	**Feature ID**: FEAT-007  
10	**Status**: Draft  
11	**Priority**: P1  
12	**Owner**: DDX Agent Team
13	
14	## Overview
15	
16	DDX Agent provides a robust installation experience with automatic update checking,
17	safe binary replacement, and enhanced installer UX. This implements the ghostty
18	pattern — great library proven by a usable CLI app.
19	
20	## Problem Statement
21	
22	- **Current situation**: `install.sh` downloads latest release but has no update
23	  check capability. Users must manually re-run install script to upgrade.
24	- **Pain points**: No way to check if running version is outdated. No safe in-place
25	  binary replacement. Installer lacks colored output and PATH configuration.
26	- **Desired outcome**: `ddx-agent update` command that checks for updates, prompts user,
27	  downloads new binary safely, and replaces old one atomically. Enhanced installer
28	  with better UX matching DDx patterns.
29	
30	## Requirements
31	
32	### Functional Requirements
33	
34	#### Update Command (`ddx-agent update`)
35	
36	1. Check current version against latest GitHub release
37	2. Display version comparison: "Current: v0.0.8 | Latest: v0.0.9"
38	3. If outdated, show changelog summary (release notes from GitHub API)
39	4. Prompt user: "Update to v0.0.9? [y/N]"
40	5. Download new binary to temp location
41	6. Verify download (checksum if available, or basic file size check)
42	7. Atomically replace old binary with new one
43	8. Preserve permissions and ownership
44	9. Show success message with new version
45	
46	#### Update Check Only (`ddx-agent update --check-only`)
47	
48	10. Compare versions without downloading
49	11. Exit code 0 if up-to-date, exit code 1 if outdated
50	12. Print version comparison to stdout for scripting
51	
52	#### Enhanced Installer (`install.sh`)
53	
54	13. Colored output (blue info, green success, yellow warning, red error)
55	14. Prerequisites checking (curl/wget availability)
56	15. PATH configuration in shell rc files (.bashrc, .zshrc, .config/fish/config.fish)
57	16. Installation verification (`ddx-agent --version` test)
58	17. Getting started guide with quick commands
59	
60	#### Version Command Enhancement
61	
62	18. `ddx-agent version` shows current version and whether update is available
63	19. If outdated: "v0.0.8 (update available: v0.0.9)"
64	20. If up-to-date: "v0.0.8 (latest)"
65	
66	### Non-Functional Requirements
67	
68	- **Safety**: Binary replacement must be atomic — no partial writes or corrupted binaries
69	- **Reliability**: Network failures should not leave system in broken state
70	- **Performance**: Update check completes in < 3 seconds
71	- **UX**: Clear progress indicators during download
72	- **Portability**: Works on Linux and macOS (darwin)
73	
74	## Edge Cases and Error Handling
75	
76	### Network Errors
77	
78	- **GitHub API unavailable**: Show error with retry suggestion, exit gracefully
79	- **Download interrupted**: Remove partial file, show error, don't replace binary
80	- **Rate limited by GitHub**: Cache version check for 1 hour to avoid repeated failures
81	
82	### File System Errors
83	
84	- **Binary not writable**: Error with clear message about permissions
85	- **No disk space**: Check before download, fail fast if insufficient space
86	- **Temp directory unavailable**: Use `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp` as fallback
87	
88	### Version Comparison
89	
90	- **Semantic versioning**: Compare v0.0.8 vs v0.0.9 correctly (not string comparison)
91	- **Pre-release versions**: Handle -rc1, -beta suffixes appropriately
92	- **Current version unknown**: If binary lacks version info, assume outdated
93	
94	## Implementation Details
95	
96	### Binary Location Detection
97	
98	The update command must find where agent is installed:
99	
100	```go
101	func findBinaryPath() (string, error) {
102	    // 1. Check if running from $GOPATH/bin or similar
103	    exe, err := os.Executable()
104	    if err != nil {
105	        return "", err
106	    }
107	    
108	    // 2. If in user's PATH, use that location
109	    dir := filepath.Dir(exe)
110	    if strings.Contains(dir, ".local/bin") || 
111	       strings.Contains(dir, "go/bin") ||
112	       strings.Contains(dir, "bin/ddx-agent") {
113	        return exe, nil
114	    }
115	    
116	    // 3. Fall back to which command
117	    cmd := exec.Command("which", "ddx-agent")
118	    output, err := cmd.Output()
119	    if err != nil {
120	        return "", fmt.Errorf("cannot locate agent binary: %w", err)
121	    }
122	    return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
123	}
124	```
125	
126	### Atomic Replacement
127	
128	```bash
129	# Download to temp file with same prefix
130	curl -L "$URL" -o "${BINARY}.new.${$}"
131	
132	# Verify it's executable and has content
133	if [ ! -s "${BINARY}.new.${$}" ]; then
134	    rm -f "${BINARY}.new.${$}"
135	    error "Download failed or empty file"
136	fi
137	
138	# Make executable
139	chmod +x "${BINARY}.new.${$}"
140	
141	# Atomic move (preserves permissions on most systems)
142	mv -f "${BINARY}.new.${$}" "$BINARY"
143	```
144	
145	### Version Comparison
146	
147	Use semantic version parsing:
148	
149	```go
150	type SemVer struct {
151	    Major, Minor, Patch int
152	    PreRelease string  // e.g., "rc1", "beta2"
153	}
154	
155	func parseSemVer(v string) (SemVer, error) {
156	    // Strip 'v' prefix if present
157	    v = strings.TrimPrefix(v, "v")
158	    
159	    // Split by '-' for pre-release
160	    parts := strings.SplitN(v, "-", 2)
161	    version := parts[0]
162	    prerelease := ""
163	    if len(parts) > 1 {
164	        prerelease = parts[1]
165	    }
166	    
167	    // Parse major.minor.patch
168	    nums := strings.Split(version, ".")
169	    if len(nums) != 3 {
170	        return SemVer{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid version: %s", v)
171	    }
172	    
173	    var major, minor, patch int
174	    fmt.Sscanf(nums[0], "%d", &major)
175	    fmt.Sscanf(nums[1], "%d", &minor)
176	    fmt.Sscanf(nums[2], "%d", &patch)
177	    
178	    return SemVer{Major: major, Minor: minor, Patch: patch, PreRelease: prerelease}, nil
179	}
180	
181	func (v SemVer) Less(other SemVer) bool {
182	    if v.Major != other.Major {
183	        return v.Major < other.Major
184	    }
185	    if v.Minor != other.Minor {
186	        return v.Minor < other.Minor
187	    }
188	    // Pre-release versions are less than release versions
189	    if v.PreRelease != "" && other.PreRelease == "" {
190	        return true
191	    }
192	    if v.PreRelease == "" && other.PreRelease != "" {
193	        return false
194	    }
195	    return v.Patch < other.Patch || (v.Patch == other.Patch && v.PreRelease < other.PreRelease)
196	}
197	```
198	
199	### GitHub API Integration
200	
201	```go
202	type GitHubRelease struct {
203	    TagName     string `json:"tag_name"`
204	    Name        string `json:"name"`
205	    Body        string `json:"body"`           // Release notes (markdown)
206	    PublishedAt time.Time `json:"published_at"`
207	}
208	
209	func getLatestRelease(repo string) (*GitHubRelease, error) {
210	    url := fmt.Sprintf("https://api.github.com/repos/%s/releases/latest", repo)
211	    resp, err := http.Get(url)
212	    if err != nil {
213	        return nil, err
214	    }
215	    defer resp.Body.Close()
216	    
217	    var release GitHubRelease
218	    if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&release); err != nil {
219	        return nil, err
220	    }
221	    
222	    return &release, nil
223	}
224	```
225	
226	## Success Metrics
227	
228	- User can run `ddx-agent update` and upgrade from v0.0.8 to v0.0.9 in one command
229	- Update check completes in < 3 seconds on typical network
230	- Binary replacement is atomic — no corrupted binaries after failed updates
231	- Installer successfully configures PATH for bash, zsh, and fish shells
232	
233	## Acceptance Criteria
234	
235	| ID | Criterion | Suggested Verification |
236	|----|-----------|------------------------|
237	| AC-FEAT-007-01 | `ddx-agent version` and `ddx-agent update --check-only` perform semantic-version comparison against cached/latest release data, print scripting-friendly output, and return exit `0` when current and exit `1` when outdated. | `go test ./cmd/ddx-agent ./...` |
238	| AC-FEAT-007-02 | `ddx-agent update` downloads the correct platform binary, verifies the download, atomically replaces the current binary, preserves executable permissions, and leaves no partial replacement on success. | `go test ./cmd/ddx-agent ./...` |
239	| AC-FEAT-007-03 | Network, API, permission, temp-dir, and disk/write failures leave the existing binary intact, clean up partial downloads, and emit actionable operator-facing errors. | `go test ./cmd/ddx-agent ./...` |
240	| AC-FEAT-007-04 | `install.sh` verifies prerequisites, selects the correct release artifact for Linux/macOS amd64/arm64, installs into the requested target directory, and verifies the resulting binary. | shell-based acceptance test in CI/local temp directories |
241	| AC-FEAT-007-05 | `install.sh` updates bash, zsh, and fish PATH configuration idempotently and prints correct immediate-use guidance when the binary is not yet on the current shell `PATH`. | shell-based acceptance test in CI/local temp directories |
242	| AC-FEAT-007-06 | Install/update acceptance tests run without live GitHub dependencies by using mocked HTTP responses, temp files, and disposable shell rc files. | `go test ./cmd/ddx-agent ./...`; shell-based acceptance test in CI |
243	
244	## Constraints and Assumptions
245	
246	- GitHub releases are the source of truth for versioning
247	- Binaries are built for linux-amd64, linux-arm64, darwin-amd64, darwin-arm64
248	- User has write permission to binary location (or will use sudo)
249	- Network access to api.github.com and github.com is available
250	
251	## Dependencies
252	
253	- **Other features**: None (standalone CLI feature)
254	- **External services**: GitHub API, GitHub releases CDN
255	- **PRD requirements**: P0-5 (prove it with an app)
256	
257	## Out of Scope
258	
259	- Automatic background updates (user must explicitly run `ddx-agent update`)
260	- Rollback to previous version (would require keeping old binary)
261	- Update notifications on startup (could be added later as opt-in feature)
262	- Custom release channels (beta, nightly — use GitHub tags directly if needed)

1	# Project rename — Fizeau / fiz
2	
3	**Status: ADOPTED.** Use these names in code, packaging, and commits effective immediately.
4	
5	Date: 2026-04-27
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Prior renames (from git history): `luce → lucebox`. Current working name: `agent`.
10	
11	One of the project's stated goals is supporting **testing**, **optimization**, and **one-shot results** — which is also why it has no TUI. The naming exploration was scoped to metaphors that fit that one-shot framing: scientists known for a single decisive experiment, famous sharpshooters, and golfers known for hole-in-one / albatross shots.
12	
13	## Proposed names
14	
15	- **Project / repo / package**: `fizeau`
16	- **CLI binary**: `fiz`
17	
18	## Why Fizeau
19	
20	Hippolyte Fizeau (1849) measured the speed of light using a single rotating toothed wheel and a mirror 8 km away — one precise measurement, one clean answer. The metaphor maps unusually well:
21	
22	- **One shot**: one rotation of the cog → one measurement
23	- **Precision over throughput**: not Monte Carlo, not statistical sampling — a single carefully-instrumented observation
24	- **No interactivity**: the cog spins, the light returns or it doesn't. No TUI in the apparatus.
25	- **Bonus**: the Fizeau–Foucault apparatus is literally a measurement *harness*
26	
27	Predates and is more on-brand than Foucault, who is overloaded philosophically.
28	
29	## Availability snapshot (checked 2026-04-27)
30	
31	| Slot | Status |
32	|---|---|
33	| PyPI `fizeau` | Free (404) |
34	| npm `fizeau` | Free (404) |
35	| PyPI `fiz` | Taken but empty/abandoned (no description, no author) |
36	| npm `fiz` | Taken — old fis3 plugin tool, last release 1.4.5, dormant |
37	| GitHub `fizeau` repos | Top hit: `averne/Fizeau` (467★, Nintendo Switch color tool). No AI/dev/agent collisions. |
38	| GitHub `fiz` short name | Some noise: FizzBuzz, `facebook/fizz` (TLS-1.3, different spelling), `fizsh`. No agent/eval tooling. |
39	| `/usr/bin/fiz*`, `/usr/local/bin/fiz*` | Nothing installed |
40	| `fizeau.dev` / `fizeau.io` | DNS doesn't resolve (likely registrable) |
41	| `fiz.dev` | Resolves (likely parked) |
42	
43	## Other names considered
44	
45	Scientists: **eratos** (Eratosthenes — clean, good story), **eddington** (1919 eclipse, mild collision with cycling/astronomy), **cavendish** (heavy collision — Cavendish Lab, banana cultivar), **millikan** (workable, less euphonic).
46	
47	Sharpshooters: **hathcock** (Carlos Hathcock, near-zero collision, slightly grim), **hayha** (Simo Häyhä, darker connotation), **oakley** (killed by sunglasses brand), **deadeye** (generic but clean in AI/dev space).
48	
49	Golf / hole-in-one: **sarazen** (Gene Sarazen's 1935 "shot heard round the world", uncommon), **albatross** (heavy collision), **ace** (no wiggle room).
50	
51	Other one-shot motifs: **ricochet**, **potshot**, **breakshot**.
52	
53	Fizeau won on theme fit + cleanest namespace.
54	
55	## Open risks before adopting
56	
57	1. **Pronunciation split** — English speakers will hit "fih-ZOH" vs "FEE-zoh" vs "FYE-zoh". Pick one and document in README.
58	2. **Dormant `fiz` squatters** — if we ever publish a Python or Node package, distribution name will need to be `fizeau-cli` or similar even if the binary is `fiz` (ripgrep/`rg` pattern).
59	3. **`averne/Fizeau` GitHub overlap** — will share search results until this repo outranks it. Self-correcting, minor.

118	Use a committed, deterministic script for the module/import-path rewrite. Do
119	not use `gopls`/`gorename` for the module path because the change is a literal

148	`DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau`. `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` is treated only as the old

154	1. Land the rename change on `master` while still in the old checkout. The
155	   change updates module/import paths, binary names, config/env names, docs,
156	   installer constants, release asset names, and updater constants to
157	   `fizeau`/`fiz`.
158	2. Rename the GitHub repository from `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` to
159	   `DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau` before publishing any renamed release tag. This
160	   ensures the tagged Go module path and release URLs are canonical at the
161	   moment downstream consumers fetch them.
162	3. Create a traceability tag named `rename/fizeau` at the rename commit.
163	4. Create the first pre-release tag and GitHub pre-release as `v1.0.0-rc.1`.
164	   The current binary version is `v0.0.8`, so `v1.0.0` is the next major
165	   without requiring a Go module `/v2` path.
166	5. Publish only new-name assets for the pre-release:
167	   `fizeau-v1.0.0-rc.1-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` containing a `fiz` binary, plus any
168	   checksums under the `fizeau` name.
169	6. Bump DDx downstream to consume
170	   `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau@v1.0.0-rc.1` and invoke `fiz`. Run the
171	   DDx integration checks there before cutting a final release.
172	7. If DDx exposes a rename defect, fix it in this repository and repeat with
173	   `v1.0.0-rc.2`, `v1.0.0-rc.3`, and so on. DDx must be bumped to the newest
174	   accepted RC before final.
175	8. Create the final `v1.0.0` tag and GitHub release from the exact commit

177	   RC with the final version.
178	9. Update DDx from the accepted RC to `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau@v1.0.0`
179	   after the final release is live.
180	
181	**Bridge artifacts**: **No.** Do not publish `ddx-agent-*` binaries, tarballs,

1	# Fizeau
2	
3	Embeddable Go agent runtime - local-model-first via LM Studio.
4	
5	[![CI](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
6	[![Release](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/releases/latest/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/releases/latest)
7	[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
8	
9	Fizeau is a Go library that implements a coding agent runtime - a tool-calling
10	LLM loop with file read/write, shell execution, navigation helpers, and
11	structured I/O. Designed to be embedded in
12	[DDx](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx) and other build orchestrators.
13	Prioritizes local model inference via LM Studio and Ollama, with transparent
14	escalation to cloud providers.
15	
16	## Install
17	
18	```bash
19	curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/master/install.sh | bash
20	```
21	
22	Or with Go:
23	
24	```bash
25	go install github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/cmd/fiz@latest
26	```
27	
28	## Quick Start
29	
30	Start [LM Studio](https://lmstudio.ai/) with a model that supports tool
31	calling (Qwen 3.5+, Llama 3.2+), then:
32	
33	```bash
34	fiz -p "Read main.go and tell me the package name"
35	```
36	
37	Fizeau connects to `localhost:1234` by default.
38	
39	### With Anthropic
40	
41	```bash
42	export FIZEAU_PROVIDER=anthropic
43	export FIZEAU_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
44	export FIZEAU_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-20250514
45	fiz -p "Read main.go and tell me the package name"
46	```
47	
48	## Demos
49	
50	### Read a file and explain it
51	
52	[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/placeholder.svg)](website/static/demos/file-read.cast)
53	
54	```
55	$ fiz -p 'Read main.go and explain what this program does'
56	
57	This program is a simple HTTP server that listens on port 8080 and responds
58	with "Hello from Fizeau!" to any request.
59	[success] tokens: 1861 in / 70 out
60	```
61	
62	### Edit a config file
63	
64	```
65	$ fiz -p 'Read config.yaml, change the server port from 8080 to 9090, then verify'
66	
67	Done. The server port in config.yaml has been changed from 8080 to 9090.
68	[success] tokens: 4082 in / 127 out
69	```
70	
71	### Explore project structure
72	
73	```
74	$ fiz -p 'List all Go files and summarize the package structure'
75	
76	Package Structure:
77	├── cmd/server/main.go       (package main)
78	├── internal/api/handler.go  (package api)
79	├── internal/api/middleware.go (package api)
80	└── internal/db/postgres.go  (package db)
81	
82	A typical Go project with cmd/ for entry points, internal/ for private packages.
83	[success] tokens: 6388 in / 297 out
84	```
85	
86	## As a Library
87	
88	```go
89	import (
90	    "context"
91	    "fmt"
92	
93	    "github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau"
94	    _ "github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau/configinit"
95	)
96	
97	func main() {
98	    svc, err := fizeau.New(fizeau.ServiceOptions{})
99	    if err != nil {
100	        panic(err)
101	    }
102	    events, err := svc.Execute(context.Background(), fizeau.ServiceExecuteRequest{
103	        Prompt:   "Read main.go and tell me the package name",
104	        ModelRef: "cheap",
105	        WorkDir:  ".",
106	    })
107	    if err != nil {
108	        panic(err)
109	    }
110	    for event := range events {
111	        fmt.Println(event.Type)
112	    }
113	}
114	```
115	
116	## Features
117	
118	- **Embeddable library** — `fizeau.New(...).Execute(ctx, request)`, no subprocess overhead
119	- **Local-model-first** — LM Studio, Ollama via OpenAI-compatible API
120	- **Multi-provider** — OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Claude, virtual (test replay)
121	- **9 built-in tools** — read, write, edit, bash, find, grep, ls, patch, task
122	- **Session logging** — JSONL with replay and cost tracking
123	- **System prompt composition** — pi-style builder with context file discovery
124	- **Standalone CLI** — `fiz -p "prompt"` with config, logging, replay
125

128	```yaml

130	providers:
131	  local:
132	    type: lmstudio
133	    base_url: http://localhost:1234/v1
134	    model: qwen3.5-7b
135	default: local

6	---
7	# Feature Specification: FEAT-007 — Self-Update and Installer
8	
9	**Feature ID**: FEAT-007  
10	**Status**: Draft  
11	**Priority**: P1  
12	**Owner**: DDX Agent Team
13	
14	## Overview
15	
16	DDX Agent provides a robust installation experience with automatic update checking,
17	safe binary replacement, and enhanced installer UX. This implements the ghostty
18	pattern — great library proven by a usable CLI app.
19	
20	## Problem Statement
21	
22	- **Current situation**: `install.sh` downloads latest release but has no update
23	  check capability. Users must manually re-run install script to upgrade.
24	- **Pain points**: No way to check if running version is outdated. No safe in-place
25	  binary replacement. Installer lacks colored output and PATH configuration.
26	- **Desired outcome**: `ddx-agent update` command that checks for updates, prompts user,
27	  downloads new binary safely, and replaces old one atomically. Enhanced installer
28	  with better UX matching DDx patterns.
29	
30	## Requirements
31	
32	### Functional Requirements
33	
34	#### Update Command (`ddx-agent update`)
35	
36	1. Check current version against latest GitHub release
37	2. Display version comparison: "Current: v0.0.8 | Latest: v0.0.9"
38	3. If outdated, show changelog summary (release notes from GitHub API)
39	4. Prompt user: "Update to v0.0.9? [y/N]"
40	5. Download new binary to temp location
41	6. Verify download (checksum if available, or basic file size check)
42	7. Atomically replace old binary with new one
43	8. Preserve permissions and ownership
44	9. Show success message with new version
45	
46	#### Update Check Only (`ddx-agent update --check-only`)
47	
48	10. Compare versions without downloading
49	11. Exit code 0 if up-to-date, exit code 1 if outdated
50	12. Print version comparison to stdout for scripting
51	
52	#### Enhanced Installer (`install.sh`)
53	
54	13. Colored output (blue info, green success, yellow warning, red error)
55	14. Prerequisites checking (curl/wget availability)
56	15. PATH configuration in shell rc files (.bashrc, .zshrc, .config/fish/config.fish)
57	16. Installation verification (`ddx-agent --version` test)
58	17. Getting started guide with quick commands
59	
60	#### Version Command Enhancement
61	
62	18. `ddx-agent version` shows current version and whether update is available
63	19. If outdated: "v0.0.8 (update available: v0.0.9)"
64	20. If up-to-date: "v0.0.8 (latest)"
65	
66	### Non-Functional Requirements
67	
68	- **Safety**: Binary replacement must be atomic — no partial writes or corrupted binaries
69	- **Reliability**: Network failures should not leave system in broken state
70	- **Performance**: Update check completes in < 3 seconds
71	- **UX**: Clear progress indicators during download
72	- **Portability**: Works on Linux and macOS (darwin)
73	
74	## Edge Cases and Error Handling
75	
76	### Network Errors
77	
78	- **GitHub API unavailable**: Show error with retry suggestion, exit gracefully
79	- **Download interrupted**: Remove partial file, show error, don't replace binary
80	- **Rate limited by GitHub**: Cache version check for 1 hour to avoid repeated failures
81	
82	### File System Errors
83	
84	- **Binary not writable**: Error with clear message about permissions
85	- **No disk space**: Check before download, fail fast if insufficient space
86	- **Temp directory unavailable**: Use `$TMPDIR` or `/tmp` as fallback
87	
88	### Version Comparison
89	
90	- **Semantic versioning**: Compare v0.0.8 vs v0.0.9 correctly (not string comparison)
91	- **Pre-release versions**: Handle -rc1, -beta suffixes appropriately

150	type SemVer struct {

155	func parseSemVer(v string) (SemVer, error) {
156	    // Strip 'v' prefix if present
157	    v = strings.TrimPrefix(v, "v")
158	    
159	    // Split by '-' for pre-release
160	    parts := strings.SplitN(v, "-", 2)
161	    version := parts[0]
162	    prerelease := ""
163	    if len(parts) > 1 {
164	        prerelease = parts[1]
165	    }
166	    
167	    // Parse major.minor.patch
168	    nums := strings.Split(version, ".")
169	    if len(nums) != 3 {
170	        return SemVer{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid version: %s", v)
171	    }
172	    
173	    var major, minor, patch int
174	    fmt.Sscanf(nums[0], "%d", &major)
175	    fmt.Sscanf(nums[1], "%d", &minor)
176	    fmt.Sscanf(nums[2], "%d", &patch)
177

184	    }

189	    if v.PreRelease != "" && other.PreRelease == "" {
190	        return true
191	    }
192	    if v.PreRelease == "" && other.PreRelease != "" {
193	        return false
194	    }
195	    return v.Patch < other.Patch || (v.Patch == other.Patch && v.PreRelease < other.PreRelease)

1	# DDX Agent Benchmark Scripts
2	
3	This directory contains scripts and config for running ddx-agent under
4	Terminal-Bench/Harbor and capturing reproducible benchmark baselines.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Prerequisites
9	
10	```bash
11	# Terminal-Bench dataset
12	harbor dataset pull terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2
13	
14	# Docker (local runtime)
15	docker info  # must succeed
16	```
17	
18	If `harbor` is not already installed, `smoke_run.sh` and `run_benchmark.sh`
19	now install it automatically with `uv tool install harbor`.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Smoke Run (adapter validation)
24	
25	Validates the Harbor adapter works end-to-end on a single task (~2 min).
26	
27	```bash
28	# With Anthropic API key
29	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/smoke_run.sh
30	
31	# With OpenRouter
32	OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-... ./scripts/benchmark/smoke_run.sh
33	```
34	
35	**Passing criterion**:
36	- ddx-agent exits 0
37	- `trajectory.json` is valid JSON with ≥ 1 step
38	- `reward.txt` exists (0 or 1 — both valid for smoke)
39	
40	---
41	
42	## Full Benchmark Run (baseline capture)
43	
44	Runs the committed 15-task subset and emits a machine-readable report.
45	
46	```bash
47	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
48	```
49	
50	The report is written to `benchmark-results/report-<TIMESTAMP>.json` and
51	contains git SHA, agent version, model, provider, per-task outcomes, and
52	the aggregate resolved-task rate.
53	
54	### Commit-independent runs
55	
56	You can point the same harness at a prebuilt ddx-agent binary instead of
57	rebuilding the current checkout:
58	
59	```bash
60	FIZEAU_BENCH_BINARY=/path/to/ddx-agent-linux-amd64 \
61	FIZEAU_BENCH_SHA=<commit-under-test> \
62	./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
63	```
64	
65	This is the required path for evidence-grade before/after comparison across
66	multiple agent SHAs.
67	
68	### Dry-run harness validation
69	
70	Use dry-run mode to validate the staged binary/config and recorded metadata
71	without invoking Harbor:
72	
73	```bash
74	DDX_BENCH_DRY_RUN=1 \
75	FIZEAU_BENCH_BINARY=/path/to/ddx-agent-linux-amd64 \
76	DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_MODEL=qwen/qwen3.6-plus \
77	./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
78	```
79	
80	### Comparing two baselines
81	
82	```bash
83	# Capture baseline before a change
84	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
85	# ... make changes ...
86	# Capture new run
87	ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-... ./scripts/benchmark/run_benchmark.sh
88	
89	# Compare (jq example)
90	jq '{resolved_rate: .summary.resolved_task_rate, tasks: [.tasks[] | {id, outcome}]}' \
91	  benchmark-results/report-*.json
92	```
93	
94	---
95	
96	## Task Subset
97	
98	The evidence-grade 15-task benchmark subset is defined in `task-subset-v2.yaml`.
99	`task-subset-v1.yaml` remains in the repo as the historical placeholder manifest
100	from the original benchmark design and should not be used for before/after claims.
101	**Do not modify task IDs without updating the version field and filing a bead.**
102	
103	Subset version policy: see SD-009 §3.
104	
105	## Evidence-Grade Comparison Config
106	
107	The pinned comparison controls live in `evidence-grade-comparison.env`. That file
108	freezes the intended `before` and `after` SHAs for the original benchmark-change
109	window plus the shared dataset, subset, runtime, preset, and provider/model route.
110	The only per-run inputs that should change are:
111	
112	- `FIZEAU_BENCH_BINARY`
113	- `FIZEAU_BENCH_SHA` (set to either `DDX_BENCH_BEFORE_SHA` or `DDX_BENCH_AFTER_SHA`)
114	
115	---
116	
117	## Harbor Adapter
118	
119	`harbor_agent.py` is the `BaseInstalledAgent` Python adapter that Harbor uses
120	to install and run ddx-agent inside each task container. It handles:
121	
122	1. **`install()`** — copies the `linux/amd64` binary and writes a provider config
123	2. **`run()`** — invokes `ddx-agent --json --preset benchmark -p "<task>"`
124	3. **`populate_context_post_run()`** — converts session JSONL to ATIF v1.4 trajectory
125	
126	The adapter's provider and prompt behavior are controlled by benchmark env vars
127	supplied by the runner, including:
128	
129	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_NAME`
130	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_TYPE`
131	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_MODEL`
132	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`
133	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_API_KEY_ENV`
134	- `DDX_BENCH_PROVIDER_HEADERS_JSON`
135	- `DDX_BENCH_PRESET`
136	- `DDX_BENCH_SYSTEM_APPEND`
137	
138	**Build the linux/amd64 binary before running**:
139	
140	```bash
141	GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o scripts/benchmark/ddx-agent-linux-amd64 ./cmd/fiz
142	```
143	
144	### Credential injection
145	
146	The adapter passes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` from the host
147	into the container via `get_env()`. A minimal config file is written during
148	`install()` that references `${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}` — ddx-agent's config loader
149	expands env vars at load time.
150	
151	If the expected key env var is unset, the benchmark scripts now fall back to the
152	matching provider entry in the host ddx-agent config (`.agent/config.yaml` or
153	`~/.config/agent/config.yaml`) and export the discovered `api_key` before
154	invoking Harbor.
155	
156	---
157	
158	## Thresholds (from SD-009 §5)
159	
160	| Metric | Regression floor | Aspirational |
161	|--------|-----------------|-------------|
162	| Resolved-task rate | ≥ 55% | ≥ 70% |
163	| Clarification-question rate | < 10% | < 5% |
164	| Shell anti-pattern rate | < 30% of bash calls | < 10% |
165	| Structured-edit success rate | ≥ 70% | ≥ 90% |
166	
167	---
168	
169	## References
170	
171	- `SD-008-terminal-bench-integration.md` — Harbor/Terminal-Bench integration audit
172	- `SD-009-benchmark-mode.md` — Benchmark mode, metrics, thresholds
173	- `benchmark-baseline-2026-04-08.md` — Initial baseline characterization

2	
3	This directory records the Step 5 procedure for deriving SD-010 matrix cost
4	caps from observation rather than from a formula guessed before a run.
5	
6	## Procedure
7	
8	1. Use the current anchor profile and the canary task expected to burn the most
9	   tokens:
10	
11	   ```sh
12	   ddx-agent-bench matrix \
13	     --subset=scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset-canary.json \
14	     --harnesses=ddx-agent \
15	     --profiles=gpt-5-3-mini \
16	     --reps=3 \
17	     --out=benchmark-results/cost-observation-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
18	   ```
19	
20	2. Keep only the `git-leak-recovery` cell reports. For each report, record all
21	   four token streams:
22	
23	   - `input_tokens`
24	   - `output_tokens`
25	   - `cached_input_tokens`
26	   - `retried_input_tokens`
27	
28	3. Reconcile cost from the profile pricing source:
29	
30	   ```text
31	   cost_usd =
32	     input_tokens * input_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 +
33	     output_tokens * output_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000 +
34	     cached_input_tokens * cached_input_usd_per_mtok / 1_000_000
35	   ```
36	
37	   `retried_input_tokens` is tracked as an integrity signal. It is not billed
38	   separately unless the profile explicitly adds a future retried-input price.
39	
40	4. Derive caps:
41	
42	   ```text
43	   per_run_cap_usd = clamp(p95(observed_cost_usd) * 2.0, 1.00, 5.00)
44	   per_matrix_cap_usd = per_run_cap_usd * n_runs * 1.2
45	   ```
46	
47	5. Run the real matrix with both caps:
48	
49	   ```sh
50	   ddx-agent-bench matrix \
51	     --subset=scripts/beadbench/external/termbench-subset-canary.json \
52	     --harnesses=ddx-agent,pi,opencode \
53	     --profiles=gpt-5-3-mini \
54	     --reps=3 \
55	     --per-run-budget-usd=<derived per-run cap> \
56	     --budget-usd=<derived matrix cap> \
57	     --out=benchmark-results/matrix-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
58	
59	   ddx-agent-bench matrix-aggregate benchmark-results/matrix-...
60	   ```
61	
62	   `costs.json` records the caps and every cell's token/cost totals.
63	
64	## Current Verification
65	
66	The repository-level automated verification uses the no-API `cost_probe`
67	adapter with the `smoke` profile. It emits deterministic token streams and a
68	positive synthetic cost. The matrix runner marks each over-budget run as
69	`process_outcome=budget_halted`, persists `final_status=budget_halted`, and
70	continues to later tuples.
71	
72	Live observation requires an API key and operator budget. Do not fabricate live
73	cost observations; commit the resulting matrix output directory path and cap
74	derivation only after the paid observation run has completed.

14	## Overview
15	
16	DDX Agent provides a robust installation experience with automatic update checking,
17	safe binary replacement, and enhanced installer UX. This implements the ghostty
18	pattern — great library proven by a usable CLI app.
19	
20	## Problem Statement
21	
22	- **Current situation**: `install.sh` downloads latest release but has no update
23	  check capability. Users must manually re-run install script to upgrade.
24	- **Pain points**: No way to check if running version is outdated. No safe in-place
25	  binary replacement. Installer lacks colored output and PATH configuration.
26	- **Desired outcome**: `fiz update` command that checks for updates, prompts user,

28	  with better UX matching DDx patterns.

30	## Requirements
31	
32	### Functional Requirements
33	
34	#### Update Command (`fiz update`)

36	1. Check current version against latest GitHub release

43	8. Preserve permissions and ownership
44	9. Show success message with new version
45	
46	#### Update Check Only (`fiz update --check-only`)
47	
48	10. Compare versions without downloading
49	11. Exit code 0 if up-to-date, exit code 1 if outdated
50	12. Print version comparison to stdout for scripting

67	
68	- **Safety**: Binary replacement must be atomic — no partial writes or corrupted binaries

101	func findBinaryPath() (string, error) {
102	    // 1. Check if running from $GOPATH/bin or similar
103	    exe, err := os.Executable()
104	    if err != nil {
105	        return "", err
106	    }
107	    
108	    // 2. If in user's PATH, use that location
109	    dir := filepath.Dir(exe)
110	    if strings.Contains(dir, ".local/bin") || 
111	       strings.Contains(dir, "go/bin") ||
112	       strings.Contains(dir, "bin/fiz") {
113	        return exe, nil
114	    }
